why: A drawing written straight into the template with its namespace, `<svg:svg>`, which `ngc` compiles to the `<svg>` the SVG namespace makes (`ɵɵnamespaceSVG()`, then the element `svg`). The walk takes the parser's name without its namespace and reads a drawing. The text count read it with no prefix and found none, so the two disagreed — and beside an ICU drawing an `<svg>`, which the walk never reaches, they agreed, and the loose one passed every point. Inside an icon stands one in capitals, `<SVG:svg>`: `ngc` compiles it (the schema lowers the name) to an HTML element named `svg`, which draws nothing, and both counts read it by its local name as a drawing — a drawing count that read `svg:` alone would miss it and fire point 1.
